We need to identify fragments that could be joined, returning their SMILES. We have formula C14H12O6, DBE 9, elements C and Cl (from isotope distribution). Wait Cl present. So molecule contains Cl. Also 12 unique carbon environments, 5 unique hydrogen environments, 11 aromatic carbons, 1 CH3, 1 carbonyl. Likely a chlorinated polyhydroxy aromatic with a methoxy? Actually O6 includes many OH and carbonyl. 1 carbonyl likely a carboxylic acid or ester. 1 CH3 maybe a methyl group attached to O (methoxy). 11 aromatic carbons suggests two aromatic rings fused? 14 carbons total, 11 aromatic, leaving 3 aliphatic carbons: one carbonyl carbon, one methyl carbon, maybe one other carbon (maybe attached to Cl). So maybe a chlorinated phenyl with a benzoic acid and a methoxy phenol? Could be 2,4-dichloro-? But only one Cl per isotope detection? It says elements definitively identified: C and Cl. So Cl present. O6 includes many OH groups.

Potential fragments: a chlorophenyl fragment: "Clc1ccc(O)cc1" (chlorophenol). Another fragment: "OC(=O)c1ccc(O)cc1" (hydroxybenzoate). Also a methoxy group "CO". But need fragments that could be joined to make full molecule. Likely fragments: "Clc1ccc(O)cc1" and "OC(=O)c1ccc(O)cc1" and "CO". But need SMILES list.

We could try to get carbon NMR to see fragments but tool error for search. Could try carbon_nmr_spectra? Might be expensive but okay. Let's get carbon NMR.
